canDo: Can narrate a career episode or set out a work process in a clear time order, using time conjunctions such as avant que / après que / dès que / jusqu’à ce que.
review: Review day 1’s layers of past tenses (passé composé / imparfait / plus-que-parfait) and day 2’s subjunctive: avant que, jusqu’à ce que and en attendant que take the subjunctive, while après que, dès que and depuis que take the indicative.
input: Read: a report on the stages of a career change, an opinion piece on “gaps in your CV” and a forum post asking for help (first pick out the time markers and draw a timeline of events); listen: a radio interview on annual appraisal meetings, a segment on onboarding new employees and a job-fair notice (take notes in three columns: “before / during / after”).
output: Write: a forum reply (≥220 words) telling a career episode in time order and taking a position; speak: a 3-minute monologue on training for experienced employees, then a debate on “promotion by seniority”.
checkpoint: Reading and listening accuracy ≥80%; at least 4 different time conjunctions used correctly in the essay, with the subjunctive throughout after avant que / jusqu’à ce que and the indicative after après que; a 3-minute monologue without breaking off.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a news item on RFI’s « Journal en français facile » or TV5MONDE about employment, recruitment or career change, and write one sentence each with avant que, dès que and après que summarising the order of events; then record a 1-minute spoken response: what advice would you give the person in the story?

questions.why: The text presents the stages of a career change in time order: malaise → exploration → formation → installation, « il obéit à une chronologie que les spécialistes connaissent bien ». B is the opposite of the article’s advice not to resign in haste; C is just one detail in the fourth paragraph.
The text says: « Ce sentiment ne suffit pourtant pas à déclencher un départ : la plupart des salariés attendent d’avoir une idée précise ». A is the opposite of the text; C isn’t mentioned.
au fur et à mesure que = as … gradually, two processes progressing in step. A (“all at once”) is the opposite of “gradually”; C wrongly places it at the end of the training.

The text says: « il faut encore compter plusieurs mois, voire deux ans… Pendant ce temps, les revenus baissent ». A isn’t mentioned; B contradicts « en attendant que leur financement soit accepté » (funding can be approved).

The text says: « Ceux qui ont démissionné dès qu’ils ont eu une idée, sans étape intermédiaire, sont aussi ceux qui renoncent le plus souvent. » B and C are the safe approaches the article recommends, not traits of those who give up.

Just before, she says « Tant que vous n’aurez pas testé le métier concrètement, gardez votre emploi » — test it on the ground before resigning. A twists this into giving up on dreams; C: age isn’t discussed in the text.

The author says « Je travaille dans le recrutement depuis quinze ans » and proposes « Je propose donc une règle simple » — an opinion piece (tribune). A: the author isn’t a job seeker; C: there is no practical advice on writing a CV.
« un moment redouté » and « comme s’il devait s’excuser d’avoir vécu » show the candidate is treated as if on trial. A is the opposite of the author’s position; B contradicts « redouté ».
A concession: « L’argument n’est pas absurde dans les métiers techniques, où les outils évoluent vite. » B isn’t said in the text; C contradicts « quelques semaines de mise à niveau ».
tant que + indicative = as long as, while (both a condition and a duration). A means “before”; C means “once obtained in future” — both change the meaning.
« regarder ceux qu’elles écartent avant même de les avoir écoutés » implies companies are shutting out talent themselves. Neither A nor C is mentioned.

The title and the post both ask « dans quel ordre faire les choses », ending with « vos conseils sont les bienvenus ». B: he gets on very well with his manager; C: he hasn’t announced his resignation yet.

« Mon futur employeur souhaite que je commence le 1er mars. Or… je dois effectuer un préavis de deux mois. » « Or » introduces the conflict. A: he has already received a promesse d’embauche; C: the two months are his notice period, not the new employer’s requirement.
« attendre jusqu’à ce que tout soit écrit noir sur blanc ». A: nobody suggests this; B is an inference from another colleague’s view, not this colleague’s advice.
« je ne veux pas qu’il l’apprenne par quelqu’un d’autre ». B isn’t mentioned; C is exactly what he fears might happen, not what he wants.
The interview covers in turn what to do before, during and after the meeting. B: a pay rise is just one of the questions; C: conflict isn’t discussed.
« Il commence deux ou trois semaines avant, dès que vous recevez la convocation. » Neither A nor C fits.
« en janvier, on a oublié ce qu’on a fait en mars ! » A and B aren’t mentioned in the recording.
« ne pas attendre que le manager aborde la question… dites-le clairement, avant que l’entretien ne se termine ». A and C are exactly the “traps” she describes.
« on ne demande pas une augmentation parce qu’on est là depuis longtemps, mais parce qu’on a pris de nouvelles responsabilités ». B is explicitly rejected; C isn’t mentioned.

« Lisez-le attentivement avant de le signer… relancez gentiment votre manager jusqu’à ce qu’une date soit fixée. » A is the opposite of “read it carefully before signing”; B is the opposite of « Surtout pas ! ».
It opens with « le premier jour dans un nouveau travail » and ends with « Accueillir, c’est mieux ». A is only the hook; C: the legal duration isn’t discussed.
« dépensent des sommes considérables pour recruter… une fois le contrat signé, plus rien ». A is the opposite of the recording; B isn’t mentioned.
« environ un sur cinq a pensé à partir avant même que sa période d’essai ne soit terminée ». B exaggerates it into “most, on the first day”; C changes the content.
« Le salarié se sent attendu, et il arrive beaucoup moins stressé. » A and C aren’t said in the recording.
« Le forum… se tiendra le samedi 14 novembre », with the time, place and practical points — an event notice. B and C are the wrong genres.
« s’inscrire en ligne avant que toutes les places ne soient prises, et au plus tard le 10 novembre ». A and C aren’t required.

« Dès que vous serez arrivé, passez à l’accueil pour retirer votre badge et le plan du forum. » B contradicts « Entrée libre et gratuite »; A: CVs are for the employers, not handed in at the entrance.

V11-01.exZh: Many people dream of changing careers, but few dare to take the plunge.

V11-02.exZh: Today, a linear career path is the exception on the job market.

V11-03.exZh: Advisers recommend not rushing things before leaving a stable job.

V11-04.exZh: For months, he felt a vague unease without being able to explain why.

V11-05.exZh: As the months went by, his plan became clearer and clearer.

V11-06.exZh: Career changes follow a chronology that specialists know well.

V11-07.zh: to build up a client base
V11-07.exZh: For a craftsman just starting out, it takes two or three years to build up a client base.

V11-08.zh: over a long period, in the long term
V11-08.exZh: A successful career change is prepared over a long period, not in a few weeks.

V11-09.exZh: While waiting for his training funding to be approved, he worked part-time.

V11-10.exZh: A gap in your CV is no longer necessarily a handicap.

V11-11.exZh: The recruiter put her finger on the main weakness in my application.

V11-12.exZh: A few weeks’ refresher is usually enough to get back up to speed.

V11-13.exZh: After a month’s refresher, she was fully operational again.

V11-14.exZh: Last week I received a written job offer from a firm in Nantes.

V11-15.exZh: He has to work two months’ notice before joining the new company.

V11-16.exZh: She handed in her resignation as soon as she received the new contract.

V11-17.zh: to be binding on the employer
V11-17.exZh: Once signed, this document is binding on the employer, who must hire you.

V11-18.exZh: For two whole years, she didn’t receive a single payslip.

V11-19.zh: to turn the page, to move on
V11-19.exZh: The meeting is over, but don’t move on too quickly.

V11-20.exZh: Nothing stops you from stating your salary expectations at the interview.

V11-21.exZh: She got a pay rise because she had taken on new responsibilities.

V11-22.zh: to follow through on a commitment
V11-22.exZh: Signing the agreement isn’t enough; you then have to follow through day to day.

V11-23.exZh: Every new employee is assigned a buddy for their first weeks.

V11-24.exZh: A welcome message may seem trivial, but it changes everything.

V11-25.exZh: His age did not weigh in the panel’s decision.

title: Time relations
